resources.string: Android may run these apps\' background jobs and alarms again, as with the default \"Optimized\" battery setting.
Android lets this app run background jobs and alarms within the usual battery limits.
Background activity is restricted: background jobs and most alarms do not run while the app is not in use.
Only part of the background controls is restricted. Use the switch to allow or restrict both.
Android shows the background state of other apps only through Shizuku.
Android did not report the background state of this app.
Off restricts background jobs and alarms (RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND and RUN_IN_BACKGROUND).
Able needs Shizuku in the background, so it does not restrict it.
This is a core Android component. Able does not restrict it.
Android refused the change; nothing was changed.
The command ran, but Android does not report the requested state.
Not limited by app standby (system component).
In use or used very recently. Minimal limits.
Used regularly. Mild limits on jobs and alarms.
Used often, not daily. Stronger limits on jobs and alarms.
Rarely used. Strict limits; no background network access.
Lowest priority: jobs once a day, one alarm a day, no background network, also while charging.
Android moves apps between buckets based on use. A bucket set here can change again when you use the app.
Android may move the app to another bucket when you use it.

Restrict sets the Android controls RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND and RUN_IN_BACKGROUND to "ignore", the same as "Restricted" in Android App battery usage. Android then stops the app's background jobs and limits its alarms while you are not using it.

Risk: notifications, alarms, reminders, sync, backups and widgets may stop or arrive late. Do not restrict messaging, alarm, health or security apps you rely on.

Undo: Allow sets both controls back to "allow". Able never restricts itself, Shizuku or core Android components, and never applies these changes automatically.

Android places every app in a standby bucket based on how recently and often you use it, and limits jobs, alarms and network access accordingly (Restricted is the strongest).

Risk: a lower bucket can delay notifications and sync.

Undo: choose Active, or simply open the app: Android moves apps back up when you use them.

Android lets only system tools read and change the background controls of other apps. Shizuku gives Able that access after you start it with wireless debugging or root.\n\nWithout Shizuku, open Android App info → App battery usage for the same app.
